clue.text: Affectedly genteel inspector in foreign car

Detective Inspector, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A snooty police inspector driving around in an imported car.
explanation.walkthrough: The inspector goes inside the Russian car's name: LA-DI-DA.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes someone pretentious and posh in speech or manner, a close synonym.

clue.text: Recipe with good nosh concocted around yard for manager

taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen words point to food, but the answer is a person: Roy Hodgson managed England's football team and several Premier League clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Hodgson is a well-known football manager, so he is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Latin woman in trouble reared in Welsh place

a woman's name

explanation.walkthrough: The woman goes inside the trouble before the reversal; in a down entry that reversal reads the letters bottom to top. Llanelli is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in south-west Wales, famous for rugby, so it is a Welsh place.

clue.text: Fierce look in old cricketer securing 50

parts.note: David Gower, former England cricket captain

explanation.walkthrough: David Gower was an elegant England batsman of the 1980s; 50 is a half-century in cricket, apt for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to stare angrily, and as a noun a glower is an angry or fierce look.

clue.text: By the sound of it, painful area's to rise dramatically

clue.text: Read about a Northern city beginning to waive church rules

taken as written

clue.text: Hands are found on this fine brig at sea getting observational responsibility

these eight letters rearranged

clue.text: Signal shown in flat, perhaps, by mayor

parts.note: a flat, such as B flat, is an example of a musical note

clue.text: Hooligan loitering initially behind museum

parts.note: the opening letter of loitering

explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' puts the L after the museum. The Victoria and Albert is a big London museum of art and design.

clue.text: Female bully delivering a tirade (not half) about incomplete journey

parts.note: a ride is a trip

explanation.surface: A domineering woman ranting half-heartedly about an unfinished trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivering a tirade' looks like the definition of a bully, but it is wordplay; only its first five letters survive, wrapped round a journey missing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a strict, bossy or belligerent old woman, which fits a female bully.

a place occupied by someone has that person inside it

taken as written
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

clue.text: Fine vision I match when dolled up? Yes and no!

definitions.text: Fine vision I match when dolled up? Yes and no!

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A fashion victim follows trends slavishly, so believes they look great while others find the result ridiculous.

clue.text: Current requiring means for steering, we hear, in a set of boats

explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, TILLER and the end of FLOTILLA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats travelling together, so a group of vessels.

clue.text: Irish label in Ireland largely promoted water

explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to supply land with water, so it works as the verb to water.
